words.gloss: relating to the mishaps (vyāpad) of the unctuous substance (sneha: oil or fat)

hindi: अब इसलिए हम स्नेह की व्यापदों से सम्बन्धित सिद्धि की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the accomplishment (siddhi) concerning the mishaps (vyāpad) of sneha (the unctuous substance).
notes: Chapter-opening formula. siddhi is kept literal as 'accomplishment' (as in the other chapter openings). sneha = the unctuous substance (oil or fat) used for oleation and for the unctuous enema; vyāpad = mishap, faulty course.

words.gloss: wind (marut, i.e. Vāta); Pitta; Kapha; excessive; eating; stool; accumulation

hindi: स्नेहबस्ति में वात, पित्त, कफ, अति भोजन और मल के संचय से, आवरण में, एक अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार भुक्त-दत्त-आम में, व्यापदें यानी गड़बड़ियाँ सात प्रकार की स्मरण की गई हैं।
english: In the unctuous enema (sneha-basti), by wind (marut, i.e. Vāta), Pitta, Kapha, over-eating and accumulation of stool, In the covering (āvṛti), on a conjectural reading in 'bhukta-datta-āma' (eaten, given, raw), the mishaps (vyāpad) are remembered as sevenfold.

text_flags.why: possible: lines 05.07.27-35 treat sneha given to one who has not eaten (abhukta) and unripe sneha (apakva, 34), which with the five coverings would make seven; 'bhukta' may have lost its a-. The printed word is kept

notes:
line 05.07.2: GROUPING: the sentence continues in 3 ('āvṛttau ... vyāpadaḥ smṛtāḥ'); the instrumentals here belong with 'āvṛttau' of 3. Read as five causes: marut, pitta, kapha, atyaśana (over-eating), viṭ-caya (accumulation of stool); this matches the coverings by Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, over-eating and stool taken up in 7 to 26. 'marut' is a word for wind and is taken as Vāta.
line 05.07.3: GROUPING: continues from 2 (one sentence). Printed 'āvṛttau' is normalised to 'āvṛtau' (doubled t, as elsewhere in this book). 'bhuktadattāme' is not clear: it is taken as a compound 'eaten-given-raw'. The seven may be the five coverings (Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, over-eating, stool) plus two more (given without a meal, unripe), but that is only a guess, so the translations are hedged. The number 'seven' is stated in the text; the list is not. Metre note: the line scans as 16 syllables as printed; reading 'abhukta-' would give 17, so the abhukta conjecture rests on sense (lines 05.07.27-35), not on metre.

lines_deva: शीतो ऽल्पो वा धिके वाते पित्ते ऽत्युष्णः कफे मृदुः
lines_iast: śīto 'lpo vā dhike vāte pitte 'tyuṣṇaḥ kaphe mṛduḥ
hindi: वात के अधिक होने पर ठण्डा या थोड़ा; पित्त में अत्यन्त गरम; कफ में मृदु। अति भोजन करने पर भारी; मल के संचय में अल्प बल वाला, वैसे ही।
english: Cold or little when Vāta is in excess; very hot in Pitta; mild in Kapha. When over-fed, heavy; and likewise of little strength when stool has accumulated.

text_flags.why: possible: the avagraha is missing; 'vā dhike' stands for 'vā ’dhike' (adhike), 'in excess'
possible: only the word division is wrong (the s of the visarga is printed with the next word); the first token also runs three words together without a space

notes:
line 05.07.4: Elliptical: no verb and no subject. The subject is the sneha (oil) of the neighbouring lines, and the line says what sort of sneha was given in each case. 'adhike vāte' is read as 'when Vāta is in excess'.
line 05.07.5: Elliptical, like 4: the subject is the sneha. 'tathā' is taken as 'likewise'. 'alpabala' (little strength) is read as a quality of the sneha given; the line does not say more.

words.gloss: stiffness; thighs; sinking, weakness; distension of the belly (bloating, standard); fever (standard); pain; limb; aching

hindi: दिया गया स्नेह, उनसे आवृत होकर, अभिभव यानी दब जाने के कारण भी नहीं आता। जकड़न, जाँघों की शिथिलता, अफारा यानी पेट का फूलना, ज्वर, शूल यानी पीड़ा और अंगों में टूटन से,
english: The sneha that has been given, covered by them, does not come (out), also on account of being overpowered. By stiffness, weakness of the thighs, distension of the belly, fever, pain (śūla) and aching of the limbs,
notes:
line 05.07.6: 'taiḥ' refers back to the causes in 4 and 5 (Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, over-eating, stool). 'nāyāti' is literally 'does not come'; the sense 'come out' is understood from the later lines. 'api' is taken as 'also'; it could also be read 'even through overpowering'.
line 05.07.7: GROUPING: the sentence continues in 8 ('vidyāt ... vāyunā snehāvṛtam'); the whole is a list of signs. Compound divided as stambha, ūru-sadana, ādhmāna, jvara, śūla, aṅga-marda; 'ūrusadana' is taken as 'weakness (sinking) of the thighs'. Modern equivalents: ādhmāna = abdominal distension, bloating (standard); jvara = fever (standard).

words.gram: ppp. ā-√vṛ, m. acc. sg. (sneha + āvṛta, 'the sneha, covered'; not a tat-puruṣa)

words.gloss: rāsnā (probably Pluchea lanceolata; probable, other plants also proposed); pītadru (identity disputed: deodar, Cedrus deodara, or a yellow-wooded Berberis have been suggested, not applied); oils (tailaka)

hindi: पार्श्व में पीड़ा और ऐंठन से जानना चाहिए कि स्नेह वायु से आवृत है। वह यानी आवृत स्नेह: स्निग्ध, खट्टे, नमकीन और गरम से, रास्ना, जो सम्भवतः रासन नामक पौधा है, और पीतद्रु, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, के तैलों से,
english: By pain in the flanks and by twisting (veṣṭana, cramp-like), one should know the sneha to be covered by Vāyu (wind). That (covered sneha): with (ones) unctuous, sour, salty and hot, with the oils of rāsnā (probably Pluchea lanceolata) and pītadru (identity disputed),
notes:
line 05.07.8: GROUPING: completes the sentence begun in 7 (signs of covering by Vāyu). 'snehāvṛtam' is read as 'sneha, covered', object of 'vidyāt', with 'vāyunā' giving the coverer. 'veṣṭana' is literally 'twisting, wrapping'; 'cramp-like' is only a gloss.
OPEN (05.07.8) [minor] text_flags / snehāvṛtaṃ: Observation: the line has 15 syllables as printed (the same in line 05.07.16); 'snehamāvṛtaṃ' (sneham āvṛtam) would give the regular 16 and matches the draft's reading. The printed form is kept; no flag added because the draft's split does not change the letters. Human decision whether to flag 'm' dropped in 8 and 16. Suggested: Possibly flag: possible 'snehamāvṛtaṃ' (ma lost; 15 syllables as printed).
line 05.07.9: GROUPING: the sentence continues through 10 and 11 ('nirūhair nirharet'); the adjectives here are taken with the nirūhas of 11. Identifications: rāsnā = Pluchea lanceolata (probable; Alpinia galanga is also given by some); pītadru = disputed (deodar, Cedrus deodara, or a yellow-wooded species such as Berberis; not applied). 'tailakaiḥ' is read as 'with oils'; 12 says 'tābhyām ... tailābhyām' (those two oils), which supports the reading 'the oils of rāsnā and of pītadru', but the compound could also be taken as 'rāsnā, pītadru and oils'.
OPEN (05.07.9) [minor] notes / tailakaiḥ: Reading check (lines 05.07.9-12): plural 'tailakaiḥ' here and dual 'tailābhyām' in 12 make 'the two oils of rāsnā and of pītadru' the best reading, but it is an inference; the compound could also be 'by rāsnā, pītadru and oils' with 12 then referring to something else. Left to the owner. Suggested: none

words.gloss: sauvīraka (a sour fermented gruel; standard); surā (a fermented intoxicating drink); kola (jujube, Ziziphus jujuba; probable); kulattha (horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum; standard); yava (barley, Hordeum vulgare; standard); prepared

hindi: सौवीरक यानी खट्टी काँजी, सुरा यानी मदिरा, कोल यानी सम्भवतः बेर, कुलत्थ यानी कुलथी और यव से साधित, निरूह यानी काढ़े की बस्तियों से, मूत्र सहित और पाञ्चमूलिक से, उसे अच्छी तरह निकाल दे।
english: prepared with sauvīraka (a sour fermented gruel), surā (a fermented intoxicating drink), kola (probably jujube), kulattha (horse gram) and yava (barley), one should expel it well with nirūhas (decoction enemas), with urine and with those of the five roots (pāñcamūlika).

text_flags.why: possible: pāñcamūlika has long ū; short u is probably a misprint

notes:
line 05.07.10: GROUPING: continues from 9 and into 11 (the noun 'nirūhaiḥ' is in 11). 'sādhita' is rendered 'prepared'. Identifications: sauvīraka = a sour fermented gruel (standard); surā = a grain-fermented intoxicating drink (standard); kola = jujube, Ziziphus jujuba (probable; Z. mauritiana is also called badara/kola); kulattha = horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum (standard); yava = barley, Hordeum vulgare (standard). Whether kola is the fruit or another part is not stated.
line 05.07.11: Completes the sentence of 9 to 11. 'taṃ' of 9 is the covered sneha. 'pāñcamūlika' = 'of the five roots'; which five (the lesser or greater pañcamūla) is not stated here, so the plants are unidentified in this text. 'samūtra' = 'with urine', as printed. The noun for 'pāñcamūlikaiḥ' is supplied from 'nirūhaiḥ' only as 'those'.

lines_deva: ताभ्यामेव च तैलाभ्यां सायं भुक्ते ऽनुवासयेत्

words.gloss: one should give an anuvāsana (oil enema)
thirst; burning; redness; bewilderment; discolouration; tamaka (named condition, probably the asthma-type breathing disorder; probable); fever

hindi: और उन्हीं दोनों तैलों से सायंकाल, भोजन कर लेने पर, अनुवासन यानी तैल-बस्ति दे। प्यास, दाह यानी जलन, ललाई, सम्मोह यानी भ्रम, विवर्णता, तमक यानी सम्भवतः श्वास का दमा वाला प्रकार और ज्वर से,
english: And with those very two oils, in the evening, in one who has eaten, one should give an anuvāsana (oil enema). By thirst, burning, redness, bewilderment, discolouration, tamaka (probably the asthma-type breathing disorder) and fever,

text_flags.why: possible: 'tṛḍ' + 'dāha' should be 'tṛḍdāha'; the printed extra a (tṛḍa-dāha) looks like a lost virāma

notes:
line 05.07.12: 'those two oils' (dual) most likely means the two oils named in 9 (of rāsnā and of pītadru). 'bhukte' is a locative, 'when (one) has eaten'; the person is not named. anuvāsana = oil enema (standard).
OPEN (05.07.12) [minor] notes / tailābhyām: Depends on the open reading in line 05.07.9 (see there): 'those two oils' = oils of rāsnā and of pītadru is plausible but an inference. Suggested: none
line 05.07.13: GROUPING: the sentence continues in 14 ('vidyāt pittāvṛtam'); a list of signs of covering by Pitta. 'tamaka' is a named condition; as a breathing disorder (tamaka śvāsa, an asthma type) it is probable, but in a list of Pitta signs 'darkness' is also possible, so the identification is only probable. 'rāga' is read as 'redness'. The line could also be divided 'tṛḍ-adāha' (thirst, absence of burning), which does not suit a list of Pitta signs.
OPEN (05.07.13) [minor] text_flags / tṛḍadāha: Confirmed by metre: as printed the line has 17 syllables, with tṛḍdāha 16. No change. Suggested: none

words.gram: ppp. ā-√vṛ, m. acc. sg., tat-puruṣa

words.gloss: drowsiness; cold; fever; lassitude; praseka (flow, trickling); aversion (aruci); heaviness

hindi: उसे पित्त से आवृत जानना चाहिए; उसे मीठी और कड़वी बस्तियों से निकाल दे। तन्द्रा, शीत, ज्वर, आलस्य, प्रसेक यानी बहना, अरुचि और भारीपन से,
english: One should know it to be covered by Pitta; one should remove it with enemas that are sweet and bitter. By drowsiness, cold, fever, lassitude, praseka (flow, trickling), aversion (aruci) and heaviness,
notes:
line 05.07.14: Completes the sentence of 13. 'pittāvṛtam' is 'covered by Pitta' (the sneha understood). 'svādutiktaiḥ' qualifies 'bastibhiḥ' (enemas that are sweet and bitter in their substances; the line does not give the ingredients).
line 05.07.15: GROUPING: continues in 16. 'śītajvara' could also be read as a single sign 'fever with cold (chill)'; the items are given separately. Signs of covering by Kapha (16).

words.gram: ppp. ā-√vṛ, m. acc. sg. (sneha + āvṛta, 'the sneha, covered'; not a tat-puruṣa)

words.gloss: prepared with surā (a fermented intoxicating drink) and urine

hindi: मूर्च्छा सहित ग्लानि यानी थकावट से जानना चाहिए कि स्नेह कफ से आवृत है। कसैले, कड़वे और तीखे, सुरा और मूत्र के साथ साधित,
english: By fainting together with exhaustion, one should know the sneha to be covered by Kapha. (ones) astringent, bitter and pungent, prepared with surā (a fermented intoxicating drink) and urine,

text_flags.why: possible: mūrcchā is feminine with long ā; the printed short a may be a misprint or a variant stem

notes:
line 05.07.16: Completes the sentence of 15. 'samūrcchāglānibhiḥ' could also be 'with fainting, and exhaustion' (two separate signs); the plural suggests a continuation of the list of 15.
OPEN (05.07.16) [minor] text_flags / snehāvṛtaṃ: Same metre observation as line 05.07.8 (15 syllables; 'snehamāvṛtaṃ' gives 16). Suggested: none
line 05.07.17: GROUPING: continues in 18 (the noun 'bastibhiḥ' is there). 'kaṣāya' is the taste 'astringent' here, as it qualifies substances alongside tikta and kaṭu; 'upasādhita' is rendered 'prepared'.

words.gloss: vomiting (chardi); fainting; aversion (aruci); exhaustion; pain; sleep; limb; aching

hindi: फल और तैल से युक्त, अम्ल सहित बस्तियों से उसे पूरी तरह निकाल दे। छर्दि यानी उल्टी, मूर्च्छा, अरुचि, ग्लानि, शूल यानी पीड़ा, निद्रा और अंगों में टूटन से,
english: one should expel it completely with enemas joined with fruit (phala) and oil, and with sour (things). By vomiting (chardi), fainting, aversion (aruci), exhaustion, pain (śūla), sleep and aching of the limbs,
notes:
line 05.07.18: Completes the sentence of 17 and 18: the remedy for the sneha covered by Kapha (16). 'phala' is not specified (in enema recipes it often means madanaphala, Randia species, but the text does not say, so it is left unidentified). 'sāmla' = 'with sour (things)'.
line 05.07.19: GROUPING: continues in 20. 'nidrā' is literally 'sleep' (sleepiness is the likely sense). Signs of covering by over-eating (20).

words.gloss: by signs of āma (the raw, undigested state)

words.gram: ppp. ā-√vṛ, tat-puruṣa, m. acc. sg.

hindi: जलन सहित आम के लक्षणों से उसे अति भोजन से आवृत जानना चाहिए। तीखों और लवणों के काढ़ों और चूर्णों से पाचन।
english: By signs of āma (the raw, undigested state) together with burning, one should know it to be covered by over-eating. A digestive (pācana) with decoctions and powders of pungent (ones) and of salts.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kātha' is not a standard word; kvātha (decoction) fits, and the same misprint appears elsewhere in this book

notes:
line 05.07.20: Completes the sentence of 19 and 20: signs of the sneha covered by over-eating (atyaśana). 'āma' is kept as the term (raw, undigested). The remedy follows in 21 and 22.
line 05.07.21: Elliptical (no verb). 'pācana' = a digestive, that which makes cook (digest) the āma of 20; the line does not name the pungent substances or the salts.

words.gloss: unclear (printed form kept; perhaps saṅga-ārti, 'blockage, pain')

hindi: मृदु विरेचन; और वहाँ आम के लिए बताया गया सब कुछ हितकर है। मल, मूत्र और वायु के, एक अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार संग यानी रुकावट और पीड़ा, भारीपन, अफारा और हृदय की पकड़ से,
english: A mild purgation; and all that is prescribed for āma is beneficial there. On a conjectural reading, by blockage of stool, urine and wind, and pain, heaviness, distension and seizing (grasp) of the heart (hṛdgraha),

text_flags.why: possible: 'saṃgānir' is not a word; 'saṃgārti' (blockage, pain) fits the sense (signs of covering by stool) and the shapes of the printed letters; metre and sense are only a guide, not a proof

notes:
line 05.07.22: 'tatra' = 'there' (in this covering by over-eating). 'virekaḥ' = purgation.
line 05.07.23: GROUPING: the sentence continues in 24 ('snehaṃ viḍāvṛtaṃ jñātvā'). The stretch 'saṃgānir' is doubtful: it is kept unsplit, and the translations follow a conjectural reading (blockage and pain). The sure parts are stool, urine, wind, heaviness, distension and hṛdgraha (seizing of the heart; a gripping feeling in the heart region is the probable sense, not certain).
OPEN (05.07.23) [minor] text_flags / saṃgānir: Alternative conjecture worth recording: 'saṃga-glāni' (glāni, exhaustion, is common in these sign lists and 'gl' could have dropped); 'saṃgārti' is not the only candidate. Metre is 16 either way, so it cannot decide. Unit correctly low confidence and hedged. Suggested: Record both candidates in notes; human decision.

words.gram: ppp. ā-√vṛ, tat-puruṣa, m. acc. sg.

words.gloss: cooked with śyāmā (identity disputed; trivṛt is listed separately in 30, so not the same here) and bilva (bael, Aegle marmelos; standard) and the rest

hindi: स्नेह को मल से आवृत जानकर, स्नेह और स्वेद से, बस्तियों के साथ, और श्यामा, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, तथा बिल्व यानी बेल आदि से सिद्ध निरूहों से, अनुवासन सहित,
english: Having known the sneha to be covered by stool, with sneha and sweating (sveda), together with enemas, and with nirūhas (decoction enemas) cooked with śyāmā (identity disputed), bilva (bael) and the rest, together with anuvāsanas (oil enemas),
notes:
line 05.07.24: GROUPING: the sentence continues in 25 and ends in 26 with 'nirharet'. 'viḍ' is 'stool' (viṭ) here; not the drug name viḍa. 'sneha-sveda' = sneha applications and sweating (sveda).
line 05.07.25: GROUPING: continues in 26. 'siddha' = cooked. Identifications: bilva = Aegle marmelos (standard); śyāmā is disputed (several plants carry this name; here trivṛt is listed separately in 30, so it is left unidentified). 'ādi' = 'and the rest'; the rest are not listed.

words.gloss: by the rule, according to procedure
with (one) that removes udāvarta (upward-moving wind with retention; roughly obstructed bowel, probable)
in one who has not eaten
in one with a swollen anus
of one who has eaten only peyā (thin gruel)

hindi: और विधि से अच्छी तरह निकाले तथा उदावर्त यानी वायु के उलटा चलने से मल और वायु का रुकना, उसे हरने वाले से भी। भोजन न किए हुए में, सूजी हुई गुदा वाले में, या केवल पेया यानी पतली लपसी खाए हुए के,
english: one should expel it properly according to the rule, and with (one) that removes udāvarta. In one who has not eaten, or in one with a swollen anus, or of one who has eaten only peyā (thin gruel),
notes:
line 05.07.26: Completes the sentence of 24 to 26 (sneha covered by stool). Printed 'udāvartta' is normalised to 'udāvarta' (doubled t). The token 'samyagudāvarttahareṇa' joins 'samyak' and the compound; 'samyak' could go with 'nirharet' or with the compound, and is taken with the verb. udāvarta = a condition of upward-turned wind with blocked stool, urine and flatus (roughly obstructed bowel or severe constipation; probable). The noun to which 'udāvarta-harena' belongs is not given.
line 05.07.27: GROUPING: one sentence with 28 ('gude praṇihitaḥ sneho vegāddhāvati'). The cases are mixed (two locatives, then a genitive); all three are conditions of the person to whom the enema is given, and the person is not named. 'peyā' is a thin gruel (standard). The token 'peyāmātrāśitasyavā' runs 'asya' and 'vā' together without a space.

lines_deva: ऊर्ध्वं कार्यं ततः कंठादूर्ध्वेभ्यः खेभ्य एत्यपि
lines_iast: ūrdhvaṃ kāryaṃ tataḥ kaṃṭhādūrdhvebhyaḥ khebhya etyapi

words.gloss: from the body (conjectural reading of the printed 'kāryaṃ')

hindi: गुदा में डाला गया स्नेह वेग से दौड़ता है, आवृत हुए बिना। एक अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार: ऊपर की ओर शरीर से, फिर कण्ठ से ऊपर के छिद्रों तक भी जाता है।
english: The sneha placed in the anus rushes with force, not covered. On a conjectural reading: upward from the body, then from the throat it goes also to the upper orifices.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kāryam' (to be done) gives no sense in this line; 'kāyāt' (from the body) fits the course of the sneha described (upward from the body, then from the throat to the upper openings)

english: There would be stiffness (stambha) and severe splitting pain (bhedana) of the waist, anus, calves, thighs and bladder (basti). Here: Vāta-destroying food, sweating (sveda) and oil massages (abhyaṅga), together with bastis (enemas).
notes:
line 05.07.56: The compound could also be read with "ati" going with stambha as well. "basti" is taken here as the bladder, a body site (standard), not the enema bag.
line 05.07.57: Remedy for the situation of line 05.07.56. No verb is stated. "sabastayaḥ" = "with bastis"; basti here is the enema procedure.

lines_iast: netre tadṛju niṣkāsya saṃśodhya ca punarnayet
hindi: जब द्वार तिरछी वलि यानी सिलवट से ढका हो, या बँधा हुआ भी हो, तब वह नहीं जाता। नेत्र में, उसे सीधा करके बाहर निकालकर और शुद्ध करके फिर से ले जाना चाहिए।
english: When the opening is covered by a slanting fold (valī), or even bound (baddha), it does not go. In the nozzle: having drawn that out straight and having cleansed [it], one should lead [it] again.
notes:
line 05.07.58: The subject of "na gacchati" is not stated (probably the nozzle or the matter administered). "netre" at the start of line 05.07.59 may belong to this sentence. "valī" here is a fold (of skin or mucosa); not further specified.
line 05.07.59: The grammar is loose: "netre" (locative) and "tat" (that) may refer to the same nozzle. "punar nayet" is rendered literally "should lead again". GROUPING: remedy for the situation of line 05.07.58.
OPEN (05.07.59) [minor] gram / netre / tat: Observation: netre (locative) beside tat ṛju (accusatives) is loose; netraṃ tad ṛju, with netram as object of niṣkāsya, would read smoothly and may be what was meant. Not flagged; the draft note already admits the loose grammar. Human decision. Suggested: optional "possible" flag

hindi: दबाए जाते समय बीच में छोड़ देने पर, गुदा में वायु रुकी हुई, टकराकर लौटी हुई। छाती और सिर में पीड़ा, और जाँघों में अवसाद यानी शिथिलता, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, बलवान उत्पन्न कर सकता है।
english: When [it] is being pressed and is let go in between, in the anus the wind (anila), obstructed (pratihata) ... The strong one (balī, on a conjectural reading of the printed valī) would produce pain in the chest and head, and sinking (sāda, exhaustion) of the thighs.

text_flags.why: possible: extra ṃ in the print
possible: "valī" is a fold (as in line 05.07.58) and does not fit a subject; "balī" (strong, i.e. the wind of line 05.07.60) fits

notes:
line 05.07.60: GROUPING: the sentence continues in line 05.07.61 ("... the strong one would produce pain in the chest and head"). The subject of "pīḍyamāne" and "mukte" is not stated.
line 05.07.61: GROUPING: appears to complete line 05.07.60; the subject is probably the wind (anila) of line 05.07.60, but the text does not say so. v/b spellings are interchangeable in this print.

hindi: वहाँ बस्ति यानी एनिमा बिल्व यानी बेल आदि, फल, श्यामा आदि और मूत्र वाली हो। दाह, दवथु यानी तपन, शोफ यानी सूजन, कम्पन: गुदा के आहत होने पर।
english: There the basti (enema) should be one with bilva (wood-apple) and the rest, fruit, śyāmā and the rest, and urine. There would be burning (dāha), burning distress (davathu), swelling (śopha) and trembling (kampana), when the anus is injured.
notes:
line 05.07.62: Identifications: bilva = Aegle marmelos, wood-apple (standard); śyāmā = disputed (commonly read as trivṛt, turpeth; other plants also proposed), not carried into the translation; whether "bilvādi" and "śyāmādi" are named groups, and what "phala" (fruit) is, are not stated; the kind of urine is not stated. The compound can also be read as "bilvādi-phala" (fruits of the bilva group).
OPEN (05.07.62) [minor] english / śyāmā: Observation for the owner: the translation leaves śyāmā unidentified (as instructed, identification kept out), while the gloss and notes both carry the disputed trivṛt/turpeth identification; policy says write it once. Owner may prefer "śyāmā (disputed; often read as trivṛt, turpeth)" in the English. bilva = Aegle marmelos and the Hindi बेल are correct (standard). Suggested: owner decides
line 05.07.63: "kampanābhihate" is read as kampana + abhihate. It could also be one compound "struck by trembling", which seems less likely.

hindi: वहाँ कसैले और मीठे, ठंडे सेक यानी धार डालना, बस्तियों यानी एनिमा सहित। मात्रा से अधिक डाली गई नली से, वलि के क्षत होने से।
english: Here: astringent and sweet, cool affusions (seka), together with bastis (enemas). By a nozzle introduced beyond measure (atimātra), from the wounding of the fold (bali),
notes:
line 05.07.64: "kaṣāya" is taken as the taste (astringent) because it stands beside madhura (sweet); it could also mean a decoction. Remedy for the burning and swelling of line 05.07.63.
line 05.07.65: GROUPING: the sentence continues in line 05.07.66. "bali" is a fold (the anal folds are probably meant, not stated). "atimātra" = beyond the proper measure of insertion.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार पीड़ा, दाह, चुभन की पीड़ा, और भारी मल का निकलना होगा। वहाँ घी, पिच्छु, दूध और पिच्छा-बस्ति यानी पिच्छा नामक लसलसे पदार्थ की एनिमा, प्रशस्त हैं।
english: On a conjectural reading there would be pain, burning (dāha), pricking pain (nistoda), and the passing of heavy stool. There ghee (sarpis), picchu (unclear; on a conjectural reading a slimy substance), milk, and the picchā-basti (enema) are recommended.

possible: "picchu" is not a known word; "picchā" (slime) fits "picchābasti"

notes:
line 05.07.66: Result of line 05.07.65. The first member after syāt is unclear and rendered by a guess; the other members are clear. "guruvarcas" = heavy stool.
OPEN (05.07.66) [minor] english / On a conjectural reading there would be pain: Needs a human decision: the translation commits to "pain" (ārti) for the unclear sarti, but sṛti ("flow, going") is equally possible, and then the item would read "flow, burning, pricking pain, passing of heavy stool". hindi: मन्द भावित नहीं करता, और बाहरी शीघ्र लौट आता है। वहाँ स्नेह यानी चिकना द्रव्य फिर ठीक से देना चाहिए, सफलता चाहने वाले को।
english: The slow (one) does not impregnate (bhāvayati), and the outer (one) returns quickly. There an unctuous substance (sneha) should be administered again properly, by one who wishes for success (siddhi).
notes:
line 05.07.68: No noun is stated for "slow" and "outer" (they presumably refer to the faults of 51); none is supplied. "bhāvayati" has no object stated.
OPEN (05.07.68) [minor] english / does not impregnate (bhāvayati): Observation: glossary has bhāvita = "soaked"; "impregnate" is a different rendering of the same root. Keep consistent or record why. Suggested: owner decides
line 05.07.69: Remedy for the situation of line 05.07.68. "sneha" is an unctuous substance (oil or fat); the kind is not stated.

words.gloss: throat; pressing; and so on; procedure

hindi: बहुत दबाया हुआ, कोष्ठ यानी पेट में ठहरता है, या गले तक आ जाता है। वहाँ बस्ति यानी एनिमा, विरेक यानी दस्त लाना, और गले को दबाने से आरम्भ होने वाला कर्म।
english: Pressed too much, [it] stays in the koṣṭha (belly) or comes to the throat. There: basti (enema), purgation (vireka), and the procedure (karma) beginning with pressing of the throat (galapīḍā).
notes:
line 05.07.70: The subject is not stated. The remedy follows in line 05.07.71. "koṣṭha" = storehouse, belly.
line 05.07.71: "galapīḍā" can mean pressing of the throat or pain of the throat; the first is taken, in line with line 05.07.32 (kaṇṭhagraha). No verb is stated. GROUPING: remedy for line 05.07.70.
OPEN (05.07.71) [minor] english / galapīḍā: Needs a human decision: throat-pressing (taken) versus throat-pain. As "galapīḍā-ādi-karma" ("procedure beginning with galapīḍā") the pressing reading is more natural, but "treatment of throat-pain etc." is also grammatical; the draft note states both. Keep the note. Suggested: owner decides

hindi: वमन आदि से शुद्ध किया हुआ, और कृश देह, बल और अनल वाला। जैसे कोमल अंडा, जैसे तेल से भरा पात्र, वैसे।
english: Purified by emesis (vamana) and the rest, and with emaciated body, strength and fire (anala). As a tender egg, as a vessel full of oil, so ...
notes:
line 05.07.72: GROUPING: the sentence runs on to line 05.07.74, where the physician is the subject. No noun is stated for the patient. "kṣāma" may qualify only deha, or all three; left open. "anala" = fire, not specified further. Reviewer (probable): anala here, beside bala, most likely means the digestive fire; the Sanskrit says only 'fire'.
line 05.07.73: GROUPING: the comparison continues in line 05.07.74. No verb is stated.

hindi: वैद्य को यत्न से सब अपचार से रक्षा करनी चाहिए। मधुर और हृद्य यानी मन को भाने वाले दे; फिर अम्ल यानी खट्टे और लवण यानी नमकीन, ये दो रस दे।
english: The physician (bhiṣak) should protect [him] with effort from all wrong conduct (apacāra). One should give sweet and agreeable (ones); then the two tastes (rasa), sour (amla) and salty (lavaṇa).

text_flags.why: possible: the print has ṃ for tn

notes:
line 05.07.74: The patient is not named as object; "[him]" is supplied for English only. "apacāra" = wrong conduct, lapse in regimen.
line 05.07.75: The things to be given (the object of dadyāt) are not named for 'madhurahṛdyāni' (neuter plural, 'sweet and agreeable'); the verb is carried to 'amlalavaṇau rasau'. Taste names: madhura sweet, amla sour, lavaṇa salty. GROUPING: lines 05.07.75-79 appear to form one passage (a graded return to the natural state, closing in 79 with 'prakṛtiṃ gataḥ'); the opening of the passage is not in this unit.

hindi: वैसे ही फिर मधुर और तिक्त यानी कड़वे, उसके बाद कसैले और कटु यानी तीखे। परस्पर विरोधी रसों के और स्निग्ध यानी चिकने तथा रूक्ष यानी रूखे के
english: Likewise again the sweet (svādu) and bitter (tikta) ones, then the astringent (kaṣāya) and pungent (kaṭuka) ones. Of the mutually opposed tastes, and of the unctuous and the dry,
notes:
line 05.07.76: Elliptical: 'dadyāt' and 'rasau' are carried from line 05.07.75. kaṣāya here is the astringent taste (it stands in a list of tastes), not a decoction. GROUPING: appears to continue line 05.07.75.
line 05.07.77: GROUPING: line 05.07.77 is a series of genitives and appears to be one sentence with line 05.07.78 (they depend on 'upayogena' there). 'snigdharūkṣayoḥ' is dual and could be genitive or locative; no noun is stated for 'the unctuous and the dry'. An alternative reading is 'of the tastes, which are opposed to each other, and of the unctuous and the dry'.

hindi: बारी-बारी से यानी अदल-बदल कर प्रयोग करने से क्रम से उसे उसकी प्रकृति यानी स्वाभाविक अवस्था तक ले जाए। प्रकृति को प्राप्त हुआ, सब कुछ सहने वाला और स्थिर बल वाला जानना चाहिए।
english: By using them in alternation, in due order, one should lead him to his natural state (prakṛti). One who has reached his natural state (prakṛti) is to be known as all-enduring and of steady strength.
notes:
line 05.07.78: GROUPING: appears to continue line 05.07.77: 'by the use, through alternation, of the mutually opposed tastes and of the unctuous and the dry'. vyatyāsa = interchange, alternation (or reversal of order). prakṛti is read as the person's natural, normal state; the line does not define it. 'taṃ' is the person treated (not named).
line 05.07.79: The subject is not named (a masculine singular person). 'sarvasaha' = able to bear everything (lit. all-bearing); the line does not say what he bears.

hindi: इस अन्तर में विशेष रूप से बोलना आदि आठ को छोड़े। ऊँचे बोलने से सिर का रोग, तिमिर यानी दृष्टि की धुँधलाहट, और छाती तथा स्वर की पीड़ाएँ
english: In this interval one should give up, especially, the eight (ones) beginning with speaking (bhāṣya). From speaking loudly: head disease, timira (dimness of vision), and pains of the chest and voice
notes:
line 05.07.80: The eight are not listed in this line. Units 81-93 name causes in turn (loud speaking and, on the printed readings, excessive sitting, riding, walking about, eating while undigested, unsuitable food, day-sleep, sexual intercourse); that these are the eight is not stated. GROUPING: lines 05.07.80-95 appear to form one passage. bhāṣya = speaking (cf. 'uccair bhāṣya' in 81).
line 05.07.81: Elliptical list: no verb (the sense is a list of ailments arising from loud speaking). timira is the Ayurvedic vision disorder of dimming or darkening of sight (probable; some take it as an early cataract-like state). 'urassvaravyathāḥ' is read as 'pains of the chest and voice'; alternatively 'chest(-pain) and voice-pain'. GROUPING: the list appears to continue in line 05.07.82.
OPEN (05.07.81) [minor] english / timira (dimness of vision): Gloss says probable; English states it flatly. Dimness of vision is the standard meaning, so acceptable; hedge only if owner prefers. Suggested: none

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: रक्त का थूकना, मक जो अस्पष्ट है, ज्वर आदि; उस स्थिति में साधन यानी उपचार अनुमानित पाठ पर: अभ्यंग यानी तेल मालिश, स्वेदन यानी पसीना लाना, अनुमान से जोड़ा गया नस्य यानी नाक में औषधि डालना, और भोजन के बाद स्नेह का सेवन
english: On a conjectural reading: spitting of blood, 'maka' (unclear), fever and so on; in that case the remedy (sādhana) On a conjectural reading: anointing (abhyaṅga, oil massage), sweating (svedana), [nasya, nasal medication] and the use of unctuous substances (sneha) taken after food (adhobhakta)

possible: 'svedanasya' is not a regular form; 'svedana-nasya' (sweating, nasal medication) fits a remedy list for head and throat ailments after loud speaking, and a syllable 'na' may have dropped; the conjectured 'nasya' is shown in brackets in the English

line 05.07.82: 'maka' is kept as printed and marked unclear; the compound is read as 'rakta-niṣṭhīvana-maka-jvara-ādyāḥ' = 'spitting of blood, maka, fever, and so on'. Elliptical: no verb, the remedies follow in 83-84. GROUPING: continues 81 (list of ailments) and to lead into 83-84 (the remedies).

The kāsa suggestion is plausible (same syllable count 16, cough with blood-spitting and fever) and correctly not adopted. Human may decide whether to print the guess in the translation; no change made. Suggested: none

The first three members and 'adhobhakta-sneha-upasevana' are otherwise clear. adhobhakta = taken after food. The compound is read as one list of remedies for the ailments of 81-82. GROUPING: appears to continue 82 'tatra sādhanam' and to lead into 84.

hindi: मौन; वात को हरने वाली विधि; अथवा अपने-अपने अनुसार विकार को जीतने वाला। अनुमानित पाठ पर: अत्यधिक बैठने और यान से जाने से जोड़ों, सिर, त्रिक यानी सम्भवतः रीढ़ के निचले भाग का त्रिकास्थि वाला क्षेत्र, आदि की पीड़ा
english: Silence (mauna); the procedure that removes Vāta; or, as is proper to each, one that conquers the disorder. On a conjectural reading: from excessive sitting and travelling by vehicle, pain of the joints, head, trika (probably the lower back at the sacrum) and so on

hindi: अजीर्ण में भोजन करने से आमविष, छर्दि यानी उलटी, ज्वर आदि उस स्थिति में मात्राशितीय में कही गई, आम को नष्ट करने वाली विधि करनी चाहिए।
